statement: Every agent-specific evidence surface (a stage's Evidence drawer, a receipts search, a standing/reputation summary) must scope BOTH its canonical evidence and its historical/supplementary evidence to the subject agent whose stage or record is being viewed. A receipt-type-only or actionType-only search is insufficient whenever the same acting principal may have produced receipts of that type for MORE than one subject agent — the search must also filter on the receipt's subject-agent tag (`agentsInvoked`), not merely the type and the acting persona.
notes: First observed and fixed for Register/Claim (2026-08-08, RES-2026-08-08-REGISTER-EVIDENCE-CROSS-AGENT-001) via the `receiptsScopedToSubjectAgent` opt-in flag on JourneyStageDefinition, threaded into StageReceiptsDrawer's agentsInvoked query param. Re-observed independently for Stand (2026-09-06): the flag was never added to the `standing` stage even though its own receipt type (`standing_accrued`) had satisfied the flag's precondition (subject-tagged agentsInvoked) since the day the seed-award service shipped — the fix pattern existed but nothing re-checked every stage against it as new subject-tagged receipt types were introduced.

The recurrence is itself evidence FOR this invariant needing a checked form, not just prose: a per-stage opt-in flag with no canary asserting 'every stage whose receipt type IS subject-tagged also carries the flag' will keep missing newly-qualifying stages.

Generalizes beyond the Guided Journey Runtime: any UI surface keyed to one agent/entity that runs a broader query (by type, by acting persona) and renders the result as if it were already scoped to that entity is the same shape — the fix is always 'add the entity to the query filter', never 'trust the caller meant only this entity'.

occurrences.defect: MoneyPenny's Register stage displayed Aigent Nakamoto's HORIZEN_AGENT_REGISTERED receipt — same operator persona had registered both agents.

Factor's Stand stage displayed Aigent Z's and MoneyPenny's own standing_accrued receipts — the standing stage never opted into receiptsScopedToSubjectAgent despite its receipt type already being subject-tagged.

canaries.assertion: the standing stage declares receiptsScopedToSubjectAgent: true, and a behavioral test (one principal, three agents: aigent-z, moneypenny, aigent-factor) proves a standing_accrued query scoped to aigent-factor never returns the other two agents' receipts.
